Title: Taking Your Innovation Project to the Next Level
Description:
This is a presentation/guide from a global FIRST Lego League team, The Lego Legions. This guide is all about how to prepare your innovation project.

In these slides, they talk about how you should design your presentation around the judging session rubric, prioritize reaching out to experts, and more. This is a great resource for learning how to structure your innovation project presentation.

Title: FIRST Lego League Competition Ready Unit
Description:
A guided unit in the LEGO Spike app showing how to make a competition ready robot. There are multiple chapters in this unit and each chapter has a lesson plan for you to use:

1: Driving Around 
Controlling movements with the gyro sensor.

2: Playing With Objects
Controlling movements using the distance sensor

3: Reacting to Lines
Controlling movements using the color sensor

4: The Guided Mission
An example solution for one of the robot game missions

5: Assembling an Advanced Driving Base
Starter bot build guide.

6: My Code, Our Program
Guide for writing easy to understand code

7: Time for an Upgrade
Tutorial on making tools for your robot.

8: Mission Ready
Final Chapter to help you get started preparing for the competition.

Title: Youth Registration Instructions
Description:
The following links are the instructions for youth registration. All participants are required to register through the FIRST dashboard.
  - Lead coaches only invite youth members that are 18 years old or older and can legally sign their consent form.
  - For youth members that are 17 years old and under, the lead coaches must send the Express Enrollment invitation/QR code directly to the parents/guardians to complete.

There are 3 Links.
  - Youth registration instructions as a coach
  - Youth registration instructions for parents
  - Main FIRST page for youth registration.

Title: Wireframe & Path Diagram
Description:
Here is a wireframe guide to the FIRST Lego League mat provided by FIRST.

You can use this to plan your programs for the 2.5 minute robot game.

Can you determine how far your robot moves in one rotation of the driving wheels? With that knowledge you can use this wireframe guide to determine how many rotations you need to reach a mission!

Title: Background Screening Instructions
Description: All coaches are required to complete the Youth Protection Program background screening. In Canada, this is done by Sterling Background checks. Attached here is  a PDF provided by FIRST with information about the background check process.
